index_intro: In Massachusetts, when the House and Senate pass different versions of a bill, six legislators negotiate the final text in a conference committee. It's the last point where a bill can still change, and it's normally an opaque process. This is the group of legislators determining the fate of these future laws.

hero.lead: When the House and Senate pass different versions of a bill, six legislators work out one final text in a conference committee. See who’s negotiating, what’s still being worked out, and share your input while they’re still deciding.

steps.p: Each chamber passes a bill and must end up with identical text to pass. If they don't, a conference committee is appointed to reconcile them.
Each chamber names three legislators, including one from the minority party. Together, these six negotiate the final text.
Conferees weigh the two versions and the tradeoffs between them. MAPLE gathers public input on what’s still open and shares it with conferees.
The final text is posted publicly. If no agreement is reached before the session ends, the bill doesn’t move forward.
Both chambers vote on the deal. If it passes, it goes to the governor.

analysis.line: MAPLE wrote the overview, the open questions and the points where the bills agree by comparing the Senate and House texts ({{senate}} and {{house}}), with the help of AI tools and reviewed by our team. None of it is an official summary from the Legislature, and it may not cover every difference. <0>About this analysis</0>

read.title: What we read.
read.body: We compare the text each chamber passed, linked above, and the laws they would change, noting related bills and ballot questions where relevant.

written.title: How it’s written.
written.body: Our team, using AI tools, identifies where the two texts differ and phrases each difference as a question the conferees will need to answer. A member of our team checks each question and answer against both bill texts, and against the law being amended where an answer depends on it, before it’s published.

labels.title: What the labels mean.
labels.body: “Open questions” are provisions where the two texts differ, including provisions that appear in only one version. “Where the bills agree” means the two versions are the same in substance, not necessarily word for word.

isnt.title: What this isn’t.
isnt.body: MAPLE does not take positions on bills. We write the questions to describe the choice in front of the conferees, not to suggest an answer. This is not legal advice and not an official product of the Legislature.

corrections.title: Corrections.
corrections.body: If you spot an error, tell us at <0>{{email}}</0>.

beta.title: This is a beta.
beta.body: We’re still testing these pages and refining how we write them. For the next legislative session, we plan to work with local media and academic partners to review and curate this material.
